turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mrs Meena Krishnan? Come, sit here, I will check the vitals before the doctor sees you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister, that is me. Sorry we are a bit late, the auto was stuck near the flyover for so long.

[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): It is ok, mornings are like that. Blood pressure is one thirty-six over eighty-four, pulse is ninety-two, temperature is thirty-seven point one, oxygen is ninety-eight percent, and breathing is eighteen a minute.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ninety-two pulse, is that high? I was rushing from the parking only.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor will have a look. Please wait on this chair, he is just finishing the previous patient.
[SEG0006] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Sit properly akka, don't keep standing. I will hold the bag.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Kamala fusses over me like I am a child. She has been staying with me since my husband died, very good girl, but she worries too much.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hello Mrs Meena, I am Dr. Raghavan. Sorry to keep you waiting. Tell me, what is the problem today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, the burning has come again while passing urine. It is very uncomfortable, ya, I cannot stand in the shop properly.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Burning when you pass urine. Has this happened before, this year?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): This burning is the third time this year. Um, wait, actually, March, then after Ugadi, then one time in August, and now. So maybe the fourth. I am not exact with the count.
[SEG0012] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She keeps saying it comes and goes, doctor. I am Kamala, I look after her at home.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): Kamala, good you came. This present episode, since when exactly?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): The burning is there since three days. Tuesday morning I noticed it, I think, or was it Monday night? No, I will say three days.

[SEG0015] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, it is more than that. From last Wednesday she was holding her stomach and going to the toilet. That is one week, not three days. I remember the gas cylinder came that morning.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Aiyo, maybe I am mixing it up. For me it feels like three days of bad burning, but she is in the house, she hears everything.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): So the burning, you are saying three days and Kamala is saying about a week. I will not force an exact day. Roughly three days to a week, that is as close as we can get.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, put it like that. And doctor, I am passing urine again and again, only small quantity, and the urge comes very suddenly, I have to run.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain in the lower stomach?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): A dull pain, just above the private part. Not too much. It is more when the bladder is full, then after passing it eases a little.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): In the night she is up two or three times. I wake up also when the hall light comes on.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): That is true. My sleep is getting spoiled because of getting up, but the main thing is the burning.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever or chills with this?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no fever. I don't feel hot or cold. At home also I was not having fever.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the urine?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. I looked, because I got scared. Colour is just a little dark yellow, nothing else.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pain over the back, the loin area, either side?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing in the back. Only the front lower part, like I said.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. I had my tiffin, two idlis, appetite is ok.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Before coming, did you take any tablet for this?

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, this is the embarrassing part. My sister had some urine infection last month and some white tablets were left, so I took them by mouth. I don't know the proper name, I just wanted relief.

[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I saw the strip, doctor. It was written Norflox, that is norfloxacin. But it said two hundred milligrams. And I don't think she took the night dose yesterday, she was already asleep when I went in with water.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): I thought they were four hundred milligrams, two times a day, by mouth. I took them for two days. The last one was this morning, then the strip got over, so I have stopped. Night dose, did I miss it, now I am not sure, and Kamala may be right.

[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): All right, let me say this back: norfloxacin by mouth for about two days, now finished and stopped, but I cannot record a dose because you say four hundred milligrams and Kamala says the strip was two hundred. It is also unclear if last night's tablet was taken. Please do not use leftover antibiotics from family again, it is not safe and it confuses the test.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I am sorry, doctor. My sister told me on the phone it is the same burning, so I thought the tablet will suit me also. I won't do it again.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am glad you told me. Now, any vaginal discharge, itching, or bad smell?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no. Nothing of that sort. Only the urine burning is there. I am not having those other problems.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fine. Apart from this, bowels ok? Breathing ok? Any chest pain?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Bowels are fine, no loose motion. Breathing is normal. No chest pain, touch wood.

[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, and one old thing, since you are asking around. Last January, at that small lab near the temple, they did a fasting sugar. They said it was borderline. I don't have the paper, and I don't remember any number, and nobody started sugar tablets.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): So a fasting sugar was reported to you as borderline, no figure we can use. I am not going to label you diabetic on that. We can leave it for another day, today the urine is the issue.

[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes doctor. Actually the lab uncle is my husband's old friend, he talks so much, and last time he was telling me about his son's transfer to Pune for twenty minutes before he gave the report.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): And today in the auto also she was talking nonstop. The driver had the cricket on, India were batting.

[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty for two, he said, and the commentator was shouting. I told him, kindly reduce, my head is not a stadium. Then the signal at the flyover, everybody honking, and the humidity was so bad my sari was sticking.
[SEG0046] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We left at eight. Reached here so late. The metro work has dug up half the road.

[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): My grandson Arjun's school bus also uses that road. Last week at the annual day he was a peacock in a green costume, and in the middle of the dance he forgot every step and just waved at me. The whole hall was laughing, and I have the photo, but I will not waste your time.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): He must have been very cute. Let us come back to the burning, though, before the OPD gets too full.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, yes, sorry. I go off, I know. Even in the shop the customers say, Meena-amma you are talking more than you are selling.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): It is all right. Lie down for a minute, I want to feel the abdomen.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): The abdomen is soft. There is mild tenderness just above the pubic bone, where you pointed. Both loin areas are not tender when I press.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Ah, that spot, yes, that is the dull pain. Your hand is cold, doctor.

[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am thinking aloud here. Burning, frequency, urgency, lower pain, no fever, and the loins are free, so my working impression is a lower urine infection, cystitis, come again. I am not calling it confirmed, the test has to say.

[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, wait, I have to correct myself, and I feel very shy about this. There is a slight white discharge also, no itching, and no bad smell. I cannot tell you which day it began, maybe with this burning, maybe around then, I really don't know the date. I said no earlier because I was embarrassed.

[SEG0055] person_4 (DOCTOR): I appreciate you saying it now. So mild white discharge is present, itching is not there, and the onset date is uncertain. With that, I cannot rule out a vaginal infection along with the urine problem. It may be the cystitis alone, or the two together, and that second part is only a possibility.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): It is only slight, doctor. Please don't write something big. I have to sit in the shop and I don't want a long story.

[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nothing dramatic. I am not starting any new antibiotic today, because you already swallowed norfloxacin and the strip is finished, and a fresh antibiotic now can make the culture come blank. So we wait for the urine result, and only if the report needs a medicine will I choose one.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am ordering a urine routine microscopy and a urine culture. Please give the sample before you go.
[SEG0059] person_1 (NURSE): I have the sterile bottle here. Ma'am, midstream, after you let a little go, then collect. The toilet is on the left, and I will label it with your name.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Midstream, ok, I will try. Sister, the bottle is small only, hope it is enough.
[SEG0061] person_1 (NURSE): It is enough. Don't touch the inside of the cap.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): At the shop I drink hardly any water, one small bottle for the whole day, because the toilet is common and not nice. Kamala scolds me every evening.

[SEG0063] person_4 (DOCTOR): That low intake will keep the urine concentrated and the burning will feel worse. Please drink about two to three litres in the day, spread out, and tender coconut is fine if you like it. This is more useful than any home tablet.
[SEG0064] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will fill her bottle and keep it on the counter. Otherwise she forgets, doctor, truly.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): She will nag, and she is right. What about coffee? I take two coffees, filter coffee, morning and four o'clock.
[SEG0066] person_4 (DOCTOR): You need not stop the coffee for this. Water is the main advice. And no more medicines from your sister or from the chemist on your own.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist near the shop already asked if I want the same strip again. I told him I am coming to you.
[SEG0068] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good that you came. See me in three days with the report. Come even if you feel a little better, I want to open the report with you.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): In three days, here itself?
[SEG0070] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, here in the OPD, in three days. If the burning becomes severe, or if fever or blood in the urine comes, come earlier, don't sit at home waiting.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): So if it becomes severe, or fever, or blood, I come earlier. Otherwise three days. I will write it in my small diary, I forget things.
[SEG0072] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will remember even if she doesn't write. Last time she wrote the gas bill date in the same diary and still forgot.

[SEG0073] person_2 (PATIENT): That gas bill is a different story, don't start. Doctor, will the culture take many days? I have a wedding to attend on Sunday, my cousin's daughter, silk sari already ironed.

[SEG0074] person_4 (DOCTOR): The routine may come sooner, and the culture often needs a couple of days. Sunday plans don't change my advice. If you are comfortable, go, but carry water and don't ignore fever.
[SEG0075] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. And the borderline sugar, you are sure we can leave it?
[SEG0076] person_4 (DOCTOR): For today, yes. Bring the old lab paper next time if you find it. I am not chasing a number nobody remembers.
[SEG0077] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will look in the brown folder at home. There are so many papers, electricity, ration card, everything mixed.
[SEG0078] person_2 (PATIENT): That folder is a mess since Deepavali. Anyway. Thank you doctor, you explained properly, I was worried you would scold me for the sister's tablets.
[SEG0079] person_4 (DOCTOR): No scolding. You told the truth, that helps me. Give the urine sample, keep drinking, and I will see you in three days.
[SEG0080] person_1 (NURSE): Come ma'am, I will show you the toilet and take the bottle back to the lab desk.
[SEG0081] person_2 (PATIENT): Coming sister. Kamala, hold my purse, and please don't tell my sister I took her tablets, she will give me a lecture longer than this consultation.
[SEG0082] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I won't tell her. Walk slowly, the floor is a bit wet near the corner.
[SEG0083] person_2 (PATIENT): Wet floor also, after that traffic. What a morning. Ok, let us finish this urine and go, I want filter coffee after.

spec.situation: Woman with burning urine again; says 'third time this year' then corrects to 'maybe the fourth'; took leftover antibiotic from a sister; embarrassed; vaginal symptoms denied, then partly admitted. Urine test ordered.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

bad.reason: Burning current; duration 3 days to a week. Episode count is uncertain, not certain 'maybe 4 times'.
bad.text: burning while passing urine (category=genitourinary, status=present, duration=approximately 3 to 7 days, frequency=maybe 4 times this year, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Borderline fasting sugar was reported, but not 'requested_by=patient' in transcript.
bad.text: Fasting blood sugar reported as borderline (type=laboratory, status=completed, requested_by=patient)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no vaginal discharge initially, before the patient later corrected herself to say there is slight white discharge.
Negative findings asked and answered: no loose motion/diarrhoea, bowels otherwise fine.
History: this is a recurrent problem, stated as the 3rd or possibly 4th episode this year (March, after Ugadi, August, and now), not just 'maybe 4 times this year'.
Medication detail/counselling: the doctor explicitly decided not to start any new antibiotic today because prior norfloxacin use could make the urine culture falsely negative/blank.
Follow-up detail: the doctor asked her to return in 3 days here in the OPD with the report, even if she feels a little better, so he can review the report with her.
Investigation/procedure instruction: nurse advised not to touch the inside of the urine bottle cap.

Past history/investigation detail recorded incorrectly: the prior fasting sugar was done last January at a small lab near the temple, was said to be 'borderline', the patient does not remember the value, and no sugar/diabetes tablets were started; it was not 'requested by patient'.
